subject: APAC overnight P1 response carveout proposal during SGT data-center migration
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T01:12:00+08:00
Subject: APAC overnight P1 response carveout proposal during SGT data-center migration

Team —

Short version: NightShift.ai requested we waive strict P1 overnight (00:00–06:00 SGT) response SLA for three nights of the APAC DC migration (Sept 24–26) because they need maintenance windows and we expect increased incident noise. They asked for a formal carveout so their ops team can proceed and avoid emergency rollbacks.

Why we should consider it: the migration involves a rolling DB failover across APAC racks; the incident rate will spike and we do not currently have sufficient local APAC on-call coverage to maintain our normal 15-minute P1 target without incurring high cost (overnight overtime + urgent EU shadowing).

Proposal (high level):
- Temporarily extend P1 acknowledged response SLA from 15 min to 60 min for 00:00–06:00 SGT on 2026-09-24, 25, 26 only.
- Require on-call shadowing from EU (Grace) during those windows with automatic escalation to a dedicated migration hotseat.
- Enable automated warm-fallback routing to our Dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1 for critical traffic.
- NightShift.ai will accept a limited credit equal to 7 days of usage if we miss the extended SLA more than twice across the three nights.
- Provide a runbook and a daily post-mortem within 24 hours of each migration night.

I've attached a short SLO carveout draft and an on-call rotation ICS. If we agree, I can route this to Legal/Finance for a one-off amendment and to Security for a quick check on logging/audit retention.

Attachments: [Attachment: SLO-carveout-draft.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: oncall-shadowing-rotation.ics (calendar)]

Next steps request: please review operational mitigation and escalation ladder below and confirm by EOD Friday so I can share with NightShift.

Runbook excerpt:
- Primary responder: APAC migration hotseat (selector: apac-migration-hotseat@redwood.com)
- Shadow: EU on-call (Grace) monitoring metrics: p99 latency, error rate, queue depth
- Escalation: on-call -> migration lead (Camila) -> Head of Support (Karthik)

Thanks,
Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez

Subject: Re: APAC overnight P1 response carveout proposal during SGT data-center migration

Thanks Mateo — good summary. A few clarifying items before I give the green light: 

1) Scope: is this carveout scoped to the NightShift production cluster only (ns-prod-*) or also includes their staging/test clusters? We should scope to prod only.
2) Metrics & verification: define the exact SLI we'll measure for the credit (acknowledgement time vs resolution time). The credit should only trigger on acknowledgement SLA misses, not on resolution.
3) Shadowing logistics: Grace, can you confirm EU shadowing overlap and whether we need a follow-the-sun handoff note? Also confirm headcount for the hotseat — do we have 2 engineers reserved for each midnight window?
4) Security: we need Security to sign off on the fallback routing to Dedicated pool; Camila please ping Ajay in SecOps and confirm audit log retention for failover events.

I like the credit structure but prefer a single cap (e.g., 7 days or $X) rather than per-night calculations — finance will want a clean number.

If everyone agrees on scope and verification, I'll start the amendment with Legal and loop in Finance for the cap.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

Adding operational detail and a short escalation ladder + runbook pointer.

Operational notes:
- Confirmed: scope = ns-prod-* only. Staging excluded.
- We will staff one primary migrator per night (migration hotseat) and one backup. I can provide names once the roster is final.
- Automated alerts: we will open a dedicated PagerDuty rotation for apac-migration-hotseat and add a separate Slack channel (#apac-migration-ops) with message hooks from our telemetry.
- Escalation ladder (final): primary responder -> backup -> migration lead (Camila) -> Head of Support (Karthik) -> CTO on-call if unresolved after 4 hours.

Security check: I pinged Ajay (SecOps) and asked for a quick review of fallback routing. He asked for a short description of the fallback flow and confirmation that failover events will preserve request IDs for traceability. I've attached the minimal runbook (apac-migration-runbook.txt).

Suggested amendment language for the customer: "For the migration nights only (2026-09-24 to 2026-09-26, 00:00–06:00 SGT), Redwood will extend the P1 acknowledgement SLA to 60 minutes. In the event of more than two acknowledgement SLA misses across the three nights, Redwood will issue a one-time service credit equivalent to seven (7) days of invoiced usage for the affected account. All other SLOs remain in effect."
I also recommend we do a canary night on 2026-09-23 with an internal dry run to exercise the hotseat and alerting paths.

Attachments: [Attachment: apac-migration-runbook.txt (text)]

Camila

Thanks Mateo, Karthik, Camila — and thanks for the clear proposal. We appreciate Redwood working with us to avoid forced rollbacks during migration. A few notes from our side: 

- We agree to restrict scope to ns-prod-* and to the three nights listed.
- We prefer the credit be expressed as a capped dollar amount (NightShift prefers credits, not multi-day usage equivalents). Can Redwood propose a $ cap? If not, we'll accept the 7-day usage equivalent but will need the invoice baseline to calculate it.
- We'd like the canary on 2026-09-23; this is important so our engineers can coordinate migrations with your hotseat.
- Procurement: please send any PO or amendment paperwork to procurement@nightshift.ai. We'll need a simple one-off addendum to the SLA.

If you can provide the final amendment language and the single-number credit cap, we can route for internal approval and sign the addendum ahead of the migration.

Best,
Samir
